items.title: Purple Haze Aurora
items.short_description: 'Scuse me while some charged particles kiss the sky.
items.abstract: 'Scuse me while some charged particles kiss the sky. One of the inspirations for Jimi Hendrix's iconic 1967 hit " Purple Haze " is said to be the sci-fi novel Night of Light, about a distant planet in a binary star system. The colorful phenomenon typically starts when the Sun sends charged particles toward Earth through solar flares, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), or an active solar wind. In the process, some particles within the field are drawn into Earth’s upper atmosphere, where they excite nitrogen and oxygen atoms and molecules, causing them to release photons. The aurora Meir photographed occurred amid a disturbance associated with a high-speed stream of solar wind from a coronal hole and the lingering effects of multiple coronal mass ejections, according to updates from NOAA’s Space Weather Prediction Center.

items.title: An Accidental Impact Crater Discovery
items.short_description: An amateur astronomer scouting online satellite maps for campsites in Quebec found an impact crater instead.
items.abstract: An amateur astronomer scouting online satellite maps for campsites in Quebec found an impact crater instead. Now, there’s at least one more—and a large one, at that—in the confirmed bin, spotted by an amateur astronomer planning a camping trip to Quebec. In 2024, Joël Lapointe was prepping for a camping trip to the remote Côte-Nord region when he noticed a circular feature in online satellite maps near Lake Marsal. His questions led a team of French researchers to list the lake area as the center of a possible 11 th -known impact structure in Quebec at a meeting of the Meteoritical Society in 2024—which eventually led to the involvement of Gordon Osinski, a planetary geologist at Western University and director of the Impact Earth database. This is the largest impact crater discovered since the 31-kilometer Hiawatha structure was found in 2018.

items.title: An Early Look at Fall Color in Canada
items.short_description: Reds, yellows, and oranges are already sweeping across tundra landscapes in Nunavut.
items.abstract: Reds, yellows, and oranges are already sweeping across tundra landscapes in Nunavut. But fall comes early in the tundra and subarctic ecosystems of Nunavut, in far northern Canada. Vivid signs of the season were already sweeping across the landscape on September 6 when the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 captured this image (right) of the Coppermine River winding through low-growing shrubs and tundra vegetation upriver of Kugluktuk, a community at the river’s mouth. A NASA and South Dakota State University analysis of seven years of satellite data found that foliage in the region begins to change in early September and peaks in mid-month, making this one of the first places on the North American continent to change color. Participants observe and record leaf color changes during the spring and fall, helping scientists understand plant responses to climate and environmental changes.

items.title: Monterrey Amid Mountains
items.short_description: Mexico’s second-largest metropolitan area borders on folded rock layers of the Sierra Madre Oriental.
items.abstract: Mexico’s second-largest metropolitan area borders on folded rock layers of the Sierra Madre Oriental. The spot where these folds nestle up against Mexico’s second-largest metropolitan area captured the attention of an astronaut aboard the International Space Station, who took this photo on August 26, 2026. The metropolitan area is home to 5.3 million people, according to the 2020 census. Along the city’s southern edge, layers of limestone, deposited in the late Mesozoic era and then folded between about 80 and 50 million years ago, form the Sierra Madre Oriental. But its channel is crucial for collecting runoff from summer rains and serves as an important natural area for plant and animal life within the city. Near the city’s border with the Sierra Madre Oriental sits Universidad de Monterrey, a host venue for the NASA Space Apps Challenge.

items.title: Dust Storm Sweeps Over Mali
items.short_description: At a time of year when dust storm activity winds down, a plume of dust blanketed parts of the West African nation and its neighbors.
items.abstract: At a time of year when dust storm activity winds down, a plume of dust blanketed parts of the West African nation and its neighbors. As summer winds down in West Africa, so does much of the region’s dust activity. Dust storms can still occur, though, as one did in early September 2026, when a plume covered parts of Mali and neighboring countries. According to Tianle Yuan, an atmospheric scientist at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center, storms like this one are often associated with haboobs —powerful dust storms driven by strong convective winds. For instance, Yuan noted that the phenomenon can affect dust over the Sahel and Mali by shifting the Intertropical Convergence Zone and altering convection patterns, though the influence cuts both ways.

items.title: Anak Krakatau Rumbles Again
items.short_description: A powerful eruption from the Indonesian volcano lofted ash into the atmosphere, disrupting thousands of flights and degrading air quality.
items.abstract: A powerful eruption from the Indonesian volcano lofted ash into the atmosphere, disrupting thousands of flights and degrading air quality. Eruptions are a regular occurrence at Anak Krakatau, a small volcano between the Indonesian islands of Java and Sumatra. The presence of ash in the atmosphere prompted the temporary closure of eight airports on Java and Sumatra, disrupting nearly 3,000 flights in and out of the area, according to news reports. Ashfall affected populated areas, particularly to the east of Anak Krakatau in Jakarta and other parts of West Java, the Indonesian Humanitarian Coordination Platform (IHCP) reported. However, this air quality hazard differs from the smoke produced by peatland fires elsewhere in the country in terms of particle characteristics, dispersal patterns, and protection measures, the IHCP noted. On September 6, the continuous explosive eruption from Anak Krakatau subsided, though the volcano kept rumbling.

items.title: The Otherworldly Geology of Vasquez Rocks
items.short_description: Layers of sedimentary rock that jut from the Soledad Basin at surprising angles have long enthralled television and film producers, including the team behind Star Trek.
items.abstract: Layers of sedimentary rock that jut from the Soledad Basin at surprising angles have long enthralled television and film producers, including the team behind Star Trek. Several of the outcrops at Vasquez Rocks Natural Area in Southern California jut from the arid landscape of the Soledad Basin at remarkable angles. Eventually this tectonic activity led to the uplift and deformation of the Soledad Basin, with sedimentary layers gradually tilting, folding, and rotating. They make appearances in dozens of other television shows and movies, including the science fiction series Westworld, For All Mankind, and Battlestar Galactica.
